standard.title: Evaluate texts using metalanguage
standard.description: reflect on and evaluate target language texts, using metalanguage to analyse language structures and features
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use metalanguage to compare whole-text coherence features, text-type conventions, vocabulary patterns and historical influences (AC9LS8U03). They have not yet evaluated target language texts critically for effectiveness, analysed texts that challenge norms, or connected language register variation to social positioning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students evaluate target language texts using metalanguage — analysing language structures and features for effectiveness, norm deviation, register and social positioning.

nodes.label: Evaluating text effectiveness using metalanguage
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate target language texts for effectiveness — analysing how specific language features contribute to or undermine the text's purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one target language text for effectiveness — identify at least two specific language features and explain how each contributes to or undermines the purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the effectiveness of texts in achieving their purpose; analyse how vocabulary, sentence structure, cohesion and text conventions contribute to effectiveness; compare effective and ineffective texts in the same genre; use metalanguage to frame evaluative claims.
wider: Evaluate a target language community media text — identify every language choice that serves the text's purpose and every one that does not, with metalanguage framing each claim
Rewrite a section of a target language text to be more effective for its stated purpose — annotate every change with a metalinguistic justification
nodes.hinge_reason: Text effectiveness evaluation — not only feature identification — is the analytical foundation for all critical text work. Students who only identify features without evaluating their effectiveness cannot engage in genuine text criticism.

response_modes.reason: Effectiveness evaluation requires a move from identification (this feature is present) to evaluation (this feature serves or undermines the purpose). Structured evaluation frameworks scaffold this analytical move.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two specific language features in a text and evaluates how each contributes to or undermines the purpose
Uses metalanguage accurately to frame at least two evaluative claims

nodes.label: Analysing norm deviation and contemporary language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how target language texts deviate from conventions to achieve effect, and evaluate contemporary and creative language use.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one instance of norm deviation in a target language text and explain its communicative or creative effect.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse texts that use unconventional language for creative or satirical effect; evaluate contemporary language including slang, digital and youth varieties; identify where texts break conventions deliberately; compare the language of formal and informal digital communication.
wider: Analyse a target language satirical or experimental text — identify every norm deviation, explain the effect intended, and evaluate whether it was achieved
Compare formal and informal digital communication in the target language — identify every register difference and explain the social function of each

response_modes.reason: Norm deviation and contemporary language analysis develops through encountering varied non-standard texts — satire, digital communication, creative writing each present different deviation conditions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Analysing texts that deliberately break conventions reveals the conventions themselves more clearly than conformist texts — students who can explain norm deviation have genuinely internalised the norm.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one instance of norm deviation in a text and explains its communicative or creative effect
Uses metalanguage to describe the deviation and the effect

nodes.label: Register, social positioning and language across modalities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how register variation and language choices signal social positioning, and compare language structures across spoken and written modes.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how at least two register features signal social positioning in a target language text; identify at least one structural difference between spoken and written language in the target language.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse how register choices signal social positioning, power relationships and attitudes; compare spoken and written target language for structural differences; evaluate how formality level positions the speaker or writer in relation to the audience; apply register awareness to production and comprehension.
wider: Analyse a target language interaction for power dynamics — identify every language feature that signals relative status and explain how
Compare a spoken and a written version of the same message in the target language — identify every structural difference and explain what each reveals about the conventions of each mode

response_modes.reason: Social positioning analysis requires explicit interpretive frameworks — students need to be able to articulate what a language choice signals about power, relationship and attitude before applying this analysis spontaneously.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Understanding language as a vehicle for social positioning — not only meaning — is the most sophisticated metalinguistic insight in the sequence. Students who reach this understanding are equipped for genuine critical literacy in the target language.
success_criteria: Explains how at least two register features signal social positioning in a target language text
Identifies at least one structural difference between spoken and written language in the target language
